about: Specialty finance company that buys and services subprime automobile loans originated by franchised and independent car dealers, serving consumers with limited credit histories who need car financing. Earns interest and fees from its loan portfolio funded through securitizations. Headquartered in Irvine, California; founded 1991. Listed on Nasdaq (CPSS). Operates only in the United States and has a portfolio of several billion dollars. B2B-oriented brand with low consumer awareness, a niche lender rather than a mass-market name.

Operates Paytm, one of India's best-known mobile payments and financial services platforms, offering UPI payments, wallet, QR code and card-reader devices for merchants, loans, insurance distribution and ticketing. Serves hundreds of millions of consumers and millions of merchants, earning from payments, financial services and marketing. Headquartered in Noida, Uttar Pradesh; founded 2010 by Vijay Shekhar Sharma. Listed on the NSE and BSE (PAYTM) since a 2021 IPO. A regulator action against Paytm Payments Bank in 2024 hit growth. Highly visible consumer brand in India, formerly cricket sponsor.

Retail investing platform offering commission-free trading of stocks, ETFs, options, cryptocurrency, retirement accounts and a premium subscription (Robinhood Gold), plus a credit card and event contracts. Customers are mostly younger US retail investors, with over 25 million funded accounts. Revenue comes from payment for order flow, interest income, subscriptions and crypto trading. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California; founded 2013. Listed on Nasdaq (HOOD) since 2021 and added to the S&P 500 in 2025. Strong consumer fintech brand with high awareness among US retail investors.

Financial technology company behind Square (payments and software for merchants), Cash App (consumer payments, bitcoin and banking), Afterpay buy now pay later, Tidal music and Bitcoin tools such as Proto. Earns from transaction fees, subscriptions and bitcoin revenue, with revenue around 24 billion dollars. Headquartered in Oakland, California; founded 2009 by Jack Dorsey as Square and renamed Block in 2021. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (XYZ, formerly SQ). Strong consumer and small business brands, with sports and music sponsorship activity.

Payments processor providing integrated payment processing and software to restaurants, hotels, stadiums, retailers and online businesses, including POS systems and acquired brands such as Finaro and Global Blue. Earns from processing fees and software subscriptions, handling hundreds of billions in payment volume. Headquartered in Center Valley, Pennsylvania (formerly Allentown); founded 1999 by Jared Isaacman. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FOUR). B2B payments brand with small consumer profile, but active in sports venue partnerships and it sponsored motorsport events.

South Korea's dominant search engine and internet platform, offering Naver search, webtoons, shopping, maps, payments (Naver Pay), cloud and AI (HyperCLOVA X) as well as the LINE messaging stake via LY Corp. Earns from advertising, commerce and fintech, with annual revenue about 10 trillion won. Headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi; founded 1999. Listed on the Korea Exchange (035420). Very strong consumer brand in Korea and Japan with Webtoon global reach, and active in cultural and esports sponsorship.

CleanCapital is a New York-based clean energy investment platform that acquires, owns and operates solar, storage and other renewable energy projects, offering an online platform for investors to access commercial and utility scale assets. Founded around 2017 by Ben Hallock and Robert Clingan. Raised several hundred million dollars of equity and debt capital; the input shows about 1.8 billion dollars of total funding. B2B and investor-facing brand with no consumer visibility.

about: Kraken is a US cryptocurrency exchange offering trading, staking, margin, futures and custody services to retail and institutional customers in many countries, plus Kraken Pro, NFT and a Kraken Wallet. Founded 2011 by Jesse Powell. Earns trading fees and other revenue; has raised funding at a valuation around 20 billion dollars and filed confidentially for an IPO. Corporate base listed in Cheyenne, Wyoming, with San Francisco origins. Well known in the crypto community and active in sports partnerships, including Williams Racing, Tottenham and others.

Canadian financial technology company offering consumer investing, trading, crypto, tax filing, chequing and savings accounts and managed portfolios through the Wealthsimple app. Targets mainly younger Canadians, with over 3 million clients and tens of billions of Canadian dollars in assets. Headquartered in Toronto; launched 2014 as part of Power Corporation's group. Private, valued at 10 billion Canadian dollars after a 2025 funding round. Strong Canadian consumer brand with heavy advertising, previous sports and team partnerships.

Australian buy now pay later fintech giving consumers instalment credit through Zip Pay and Zip Money at online and in-store retailers in Australia, New Zealand and, importantly, the United States, where it is the main growth market. Earns merchant and customer fees, with millions of users and thousands of merchants. Headquartered in Sydney; founded 2013. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ZIP). Recognised consumer finance brand in Australia and growing in the US, and has used sports partnerships.

Payments company operating the Epay prepaid top-up, Ria money transfer and Euronet ATM and card processing businesses, plus the Dandelion network, moving money and digital value across 200 countries. Customers are consumers sending remittances, banks, mobile operators and retailers, with revenue near 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in Leawood, Kansas; founded 1994. Listed on Nasdaq (EEFT). Ria is a recognised remittance brand in migrant communities, with some sports sponsorship.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies is a US-listed company, now run as an ether treasury company holding one of the largest corporate stashes of ETH, after earlier work on bitcoin mining with immersion cooling. Based in Las Vegas, Nevada, chaired by Tom Lee of Fundstrat. Traded on NYSE American (BMNR). Funding shown is about 1.5 billion dollars. Investor-facing business with little consumer awareness.

about: FalconX is a digital asset prime broker offering trading, lending, custody and derivatives for crypto institutions such as funds, banks and miners, and acquired 21Shares in 2025. Founded 2018 by Raghu Yarlagadda and based in San Mateo, California. Raised about 1.5 billion dollars in funding and valued at 8 billion dollars. Privately held. Institutional B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

Clip is a Mexican payments and commerce company known for its card-reader terminals and point of sale tools that let small businesses accept card payments, plus business loans and online payments. Customers are merchants of all sizes across Mexico. Headquartered in Mexico City; founded 2012. Venture backed with about 1.1 billion dollars raised including debt facilities. Private. Well known to small business owners in Mexico, with limited reach with consumers elsewhere.

about: Forward Financing is a US alternative lender to small businesses, offering merchant cash advances, term loans and lines of credit that are repaid from daily sales. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2012. Funded through capital partners with total funding shown at about 1.1 billion dollars. Customers are small retailers, restaurants and service firms. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

about: FundPark is a Hong Kong-based fintech providing supply chain and working capital financing to small and medium sized exporters and online sellers in Asia, using data and automation for credit decisions. Located in Kwun Tong, Kowloon; funding shown at about 1.1 billion dollars largely from debt facilities. Customers are SMEs. B2B finance brand with no meaningful consumer awareness. Limited public information - check before outreach.

about: ID Finance is a Spanish fintech lender using machine learning to offer online consumer loans and credit cards in Spain, Mexico, Brazil, Poland and the Philippines, through brands such as MoneyMan and Creditea. Customers are retail borrowers who apply by app. Headquartered in Barcelona; founded 2012. Private, with funding of about 900 million dollars including debt. Active marketing in consumer finance but little general brand recognition.

about: IIFL Home Finance is an Indian housing finance company, part of the IIFL group, offering home loans, loans against property and construction finance mainly to salaried and self-employed borrowers in smaller cities. Operates through a nationwide branch network. Headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana (the registered office is in Mumbai). Subsidiary of IIFL Finance, listed on the NSE and BSE, with funding shown at about 940 million dollars. Moderate brand awareness in India.

about: Lendo is a Saudi lending marketplace that connects SMEs and digital businesses with alternative finance, based in Riyadh. Offers working capital and receivable-backed financing and has been backed by regional funds. Funding shown at around 975 million dollars, including debt facilities. B2B fintech brand, with limited consumer awareness outside the Saudi startup scene. Limited public information - check before outreach.

about: Corebridge Financial is a US provider of retirement solutions and life insurance, selling annuities, group retirement plans and life insurance through advisers, banks and workplace channels. It manages assets in the hundreds of billions of dollars. Headquartered in Houston, Texas; formerly AIG's Life & Retirement unit, IPO in 2022 on the New York Stock Exchange (CRBG). AIG and Nippon Life are major shareholders. Brand awareness is moderate.

about: IREN, formerly Iris Energy, owns data centers powered by renewable energy for bitcoin mining and AI cloud services, supplying GPU capacity to AI customers such as Microsoft under a 2025 contract of about 9.7 billion dollars. Operates sites in Canada and Texas. Headquartered in Sydney, Australia; founded 2018. Listed on Nasdaq (IREN). B2B infrastructure operator, tied to bitcoin and AI markets, with little consumer brand profile.

Global professional services firm in risk, strategy and people, owning Marsh (insurance broking), Guy Carpenter (reinsurance), Mercer (human resources and pensions) and Oliver Wyman (consulting). Customers are corporations, governments and institutions, with revenue near 24 billion dollars and about 90,000 employees in 130 countries. Headquartered in New York; formed 1905. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (MMC). B2B brand, well known in business, with sports sponsorship such as team partnerships.

Shriram Finance is one of India's largest non-bank lenders, formed in 2022 by merging Shriram Transport Finance and Shriram City Union Finance, with loans for commercial vehicles, small businesses, two-wheelers, gold and personal borrowers. Operates through thousands of branches with assets of about 2.5 trillion rupees and more. Headquartered in Mumbai (registered in Chennai). Listed on the NSE and BSE (SHRIRAMFIN). Well known across smaller Indian towns and trucking communities.

State Street is a major US custody bank and asset manager, providing asset servicing, investment management through State Street Investment Management (SPDR ETFs) and alpha platform services. Customers are institutional investors, with around 50 trillion dollars under custody and administration and revenue near 22 billion dollars. Headquartered in Boston; founded 1792. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (STT). Institutional brand known to finance professionals, with the SPDR ETF brand better known to retail investors; has sponsored events.

TAQA, Abu Dhabi National Energy Company, is a state-controlled utility group in water and power generation, transmission and distribution, with investments in oil and gas, renewables, and international assets in Morocco, Ghana, India, the UK and the US. Serves governments and utilities. Headquartered in Abu Dhabi; listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (TAQA). Majority owned by ADQ and the Abu Dhabi government, with Abu Dhabi National Energy Company named in the Gulf. Utility brand with moderate regional awareness.

Ares Capital Corporation is the largest US publicly traded business development company, lending to middle market companies through first and second lien loans and equity investments, managed by Ares Management. Portfolio is near 25 billion dollars. Registered in New York, with the input showing London. Listed on Nasdaq (ARCC). Customers are private middle-market firms; investors are mostly income-seeking. B2B financial brand with no consumer awareness.

about: China Galaxy Securities is a major Chinese state-controlled brokerage and investment bank offering securities trading, wealth management, investment banking, asset management and futures services through many branches. Headquartered in Beijing; formed in 2007 from Galaxy Securities. Listed in Hong Kong (6881) and Shanghai (601881), with Central Huijin as its main shareholder. Financial brand with strong awareness among Chinese retail investors, limited global profile.

CITIC Securities is China's largest investment bank and brokerage by assets, with services in underwriting, brokerage, asset management, trading and research, and international operations after buying CLSA. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 1995. Listed in Shanghai (600030) and Hong Kong (6030), part of the state-owned CITIC group. Strong brand within Chinese finance, limited consumer sports marketing.

CleanSpark is a US bitcoin miner that runs mining data centers in Georgia, Tennessee and Wyoming and has been expanding into AI and high-performance computing, with a strategy of owning its sites and power. Headquartered in Henderson, Nevada (input) and listed on Nasdaq (CLSK). Earnings track bitcoin prices and hashrate. Little mass consumer awareness, but known to crypto investors, with sponsorship deals in sports.

Credit Acceptance is a US consumer finance company that provides financing for used car buyers with bad or limited credit through independent and franchised dealers, earning interest on its loan portfolio and dealer fees. Headquartered in Southfield, Michigan; founded 1972. Listed on Nasdaq (CACC). Loan book around 8 billion dollars. B2B dealer-facing brand with little consumer awareness.

Enel Finance International is the Dutch-registered financing subsidiary of Enel, the Italian energy group, raising debt in the international bond markets to fund the group's utility and renewable energy operations. Based in Amsterdam. It is not a standalone consumer business and has no sponsorship profile of its own. The relevant brand is the parent Enel, a major listed utility with global sponsorship experience including Formula E. Limited stand-alone information.

about: Fairfax Financial Holdings is a Canadian insurance and investment holding company led by Prem Watsa, owning property and casualty insurers such as Odyssey Group, Allied World, Northbridge and Brit, and stakes in Eurobank, Blackberry and others. Earns premiums and investment returns, with revenue near 30 billion dollars. Headquartered in Toronto; founded 1985. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (FFH). B2B insurance group with low consumer awareness.

Fiserv is a financial technology provider offering core banking processing, payments (Clover merchant platform, First Data), digital banking and card issuing to banks, credit unions and merchants. Revenue near 20 billion dollars with about 38,000 employees. Headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; founded 1984. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FI, now FISV). Fiserv's stock dropped heavily in 2025 on weaker guidance. B2B brand, recognised via Fiserv Forum naming rights for the Milwaukee Bucks arena.

FNZ is a wealth management platform provider that supplies technology and operations to banks, insurers and asset managers, administering investment accounts for millions of end customers in many countries. Headquartered in London with roots in New Zealand; founded 2003. Privately held, with investors including Generation Investment Management, CDPQ and Oakley; employees hold stakes. Valued at about 20 billion dollars in 2022 and recapitalised later. B2B finance brand with low consumer awareness.

Freddie Mac (Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation) is a US government-sponsored enterprise that buys mortgages from lenders, guarantees and packages them into securities to support the housing finance market. Customers are banks and mortgage lenders; indirectly homebuyers. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia; chartered 1970. Under federal conservatorship since 2008, with shares traded over the counter (FMCC); discussions of a public offering of Fannie and Freddie arose in 2025. Moderately known to US homebuyers.

FS/KKR Advisor is the investment adviser behind FS KKR Capital Corp, a publicly traded business development company that lends to US middle market companies, jointly managed by Future Standard (FS Investments) and KKR Credit. Based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Funding shown is about 6.2 billion dollars. Customers are private companies, and investors are income-oriented. Financial brand with no consumer awareness.

about: Funding Circle is a UK-based online lending marketplace for small businesses, which borrow from institutional and retail investors through loans of up to 500,000 pounds in the UK and via US business loans previously. Headquartered in London; founded 2010. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (FCH) since 2018. Has scaled down some international operations and now focuses on the UK. Known to UK small-business owners, with modest consumer brand profile.

Imprint is a US fintech that designs and runs co-branded credit cards for retailers and consumer brands, such as Rakuten, Brooks Brothers, Fanatics, Booking.com and Fleet Farm, handling underwriting, rewards and servicing. Headquartered in New York; founded 2021. Raised about 2.9 billion dollars including debt facilities. Private. B2B partner brand, little consumer awareness itself; the end consumers see the partner's name.

about: Manulife Financial is Canada's largest life insurer, offering life and health insurance, wealth and asset management and retirement products to individuals and institutions in Canada, the US (John Hancock) and Asia, with assets under management above 1 trillion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Toronto; founded 1887. Listed on the Toronto and New York exchanges (MFC). Well-known consumer financial brand and active sponsor of sports and events.

MARA Holdings, formerly Marathon Digital, is one of the largest publicly traded bitcoin miners and a large corporate holder of bitcoin, operating mining sites in North America and abroad and exploring AI and energy projects. Headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida (input), listed on Nasdaq (MARA). Revenue tracks bitcoin prices. Known among crypto investors, with little mass-consumer awareness.

Mitsubishi Corporation is Japan's largest general trading company, with businesses in natural gas, industrial materials, chemicals, mobility, food and consumer products (including the Lawson convenience store chain), power, and in metals. Revenue near 17 trillion yen. Headquartered in Tokyo; founded 1950 after the post-war breakup of the Mitsubishi zaibatsu. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (8058), with Berkshire Hathaway as a notable holder. Large B2B conglomerate with strong Japanese brand recognition.

Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold loan company, lending against household gold jewellery through more than 5,000 branches, plus microfinance, home loans, money transfer and insurance via subsidiaries. Customers are low and middle income households. Headquartered in Kochi, Kerala (the input shows New Delhi). Listed on the NSE and BSE (MUTHOOTFIN), run by the Muthoot family. Well known across India with cricket and celebrity-led advertising, including a sports sponsor history.

OneMain Financial is a US consumer lender providing personal installment loans, auto-secured loans and credit cards to non-prime borrowers, through branches and online, with a loan portfolio near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Evansville, Indiana, with the input showing Baltimore. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (OMF); the former Springleaf and OneMain merged in 2015 (previously Citigroup's CitiFinancial). Moderate consumer awareness, advertising via branches and sponsorships.

Rithm Capital is a US asset manager and real estate investor focused on mortgage servicing rights (Newrez), origination, single-family rental, and acquired Sculptor Capital (2023) and Paramount Group. Revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; formerly New Residential. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RITM). B2B and investor brand, but its Newrez business serves consumers.

Sumitomo Corporation is a Japanese general trading company with businesses in metals, transport and construction systems, infrastructure, media and digital, lifestyle retail (Summit supermarkets) and mineral resources. Revenue near 6 trillion yen. Headquartered in Tokyo; founded 1919. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (8053), part of the Sumitomo keiretsu. B2B conglomerate with strong Japanese recognition and limited consumer sponsorship.

HASI (HA Sustainable Infrastructure Capital) is a US investor that provides capital to climate solutions projects such as solar, wind, storage, efficiency and fuel cells, earning interest and income from its portfolio of roughly 6 billion dollars. Headquartered in Annapolis, Maryland; formed 2013, after a spin from a bank advisor. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HASI). B2B financier with no consumer awareness.

AvidXchange provides accounts payable automation and payment software for mid-market businesses in the US, handling invoices, approvals and payments, and a network of suppliers. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina; founded 2000. Listed on Nasdaq (AVDX) in 2021 and taken private by TPG in 2025 in a deal valued at about 2.2 billion dollars. B2B brand with no consumer awareness, though it had sponsored sports and naming rights in Charlotte.

Hometap is a US fintech that offers homeowners cash in exchange for a share of their home's future value through home equity investments, instead of loans, with no monthly payments. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2017. Raised significant funding, shown as about 1 billion dollars including capital for investment. Private. Consumer-facing brand with modest awareness among homeowners.

about: MPOWER Financing provides student loans without a cosigner or collateral to international students and immigrants studying in the US and Canada, plus scholarships and immigration support. Headquartered in Washington, DC; founded 2014 by Manu Smadja and Isabelle Bronsert. Funding shown is about 940 million dollars, mostly debt capital. Private. Well known among international students, little broader awareness.

Nakamoto Holdings is a Utah-based company created by David Bailey's Nakamoto bitcoin treasury strategy through a 2025 merger with healthcare company KindlyMD (Murray, Utah), which holds a large bitcoin balance and plans to buy more. Listed on Nasdaq (NAKA). Funding shown is about 965 million dollars. Investor-focused brand, with no wider consumer recognition.

about: Remitly is a digital remittance company allowing migrants to send money from the US, Canada, UK, EU, Australia and other countries to over 170 receiving countries through a mobile app, with fast transfers and transparent fees. Revenue near 1.6 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington; founded 2011. Listed on Nasdaq (RELY) since 2021. Strong consumer brand in migrant communities and active in sports sponsorship.

Worldline is a French payments and transactional services company, processing card payments for merchants, banks and public sector clients in Europe and beyond, with terminals, e-commerce acquiring and digital banking. Revenue near 4.6 billion euros. Headquartered in Puteaux near Paris; spun out of Atos in 2014 and listed on Euronext Paris (WLN). Working through financial pressure and restructuring in 2025. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness, though it has sponsored cycling and events.

Zepz (formerly Sendwave and WorldRemit, merged 2021) is a London-based digital money-transfer company. Its apps, WorldRemit and Sendwave, let migrants send money from countries such as the UK, US, Canada and Europe to mobile wallets, bank accounts and cash pickup in Africa, Asia and Latin America. It earns fees and foreign-exchange margin on transfers, serving millions of retail customers across roughly 130 countries. Privately held and venture-backed, with over $1bn raised. Consumer fintech brand with solid awareness within diaspora communities, little mainstream profile.

Acrisure is a Grand Rapids, Michigan financial services firm that began as an insurance broker and has grown through hundreds of acquisitions. It offers insurance brokerage, reinsurance, employee benefits, asset and wealth management, cyber services, real estate services and AI-driven insurance technology to businesses and individuals worldwide. It reports revenue of several billion dollars and tens of thousands of staff in over 100 countries. Privately held, backed by investors including Blackstone, Bain and Mubadala. Acrisure holds naming rights to Acrisure Stadium, the Pittsburgh Steelers' home, and is active in sports sponsorship.

Affirm is a San Francisco fintech offering buy-now-pay-later loans at online and in-store checkouts. It partners with merchants such as Amazon, Shopify, Walmart and Apple, and earns merchant fees, interest on loans and interchange from its debit card. Customers are US, Canadian and UK shoppers, and the company reports annual gross merchandise volume above $30bn. Founded in 2012 by Max Levchin, it listed on the Nasdaq (AFRM) in 2021. Consumer-facing brand with strong US awareness through checkout buttons; it has run sports sponsorships including the NFL and Premier League deals.

Claritev Corporation is the 2025 rebrand of MultiPlan, a McLean, Virginia healthcare cost management and payments technology company. It sells analytics-based claims repricing and network-access services to health insurers, self-funded employers and third-party administrators, taking fees tied to savings. It is listed on the NYSE (CTEV) and carries heavy debt following a 2021 SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp III. B2B healthcare technology provider with no consumer brand awareness.

Freepoint Commodities is a Stamford, Connecticut commodity merchant that trades and markets physical energy, metals and agricultural products, including crude oil, refined products, natural gas liquids, metals and concentrates. Customers are producers, refiners and industrial buyers worldwide, and it earns trading margins and logistics fees, with offices across Europe, Asia and the Americas. Founded in 2012. Privately held, with funding including a large investment from Hartree Partners and others. B2B trading house with little public consumer awareness.

Nexi is a Milan-based European payments company (PayTech), formed by the merger of Nexi, Nets and SIA. It provides merchant acquiring, card issuing and processing, digital banking infrastructure and online payment services to banks, merchants and businesses across Italy, the Nordics, the DACH region and Central and Eastern Europe. It serves millions of merchants and has annual revenue around EUR3.5bn. Listed on Borsa Italiana (NEXI) with investors including Hellman and Friedman and Bain Capital. Mostly B2B, though the logo is visible at payment terminals and through sponsorships.

PhonePe is a Bengaluru-based Indian digital payments and financial services platform built on the UPI system, with a leading market share of UPI transactions. Its app serves several hundred million registered users and millions of merchants, offering payments, wealth products, insurance distribution, lending referrals and merchant devices. Majority-owned by Walmart after Flipkart's 2016 acquisition and separated from Flipkart in 2022. Private, and preparing a stock market listing in India. Strong consumer brand in India with big cricket, IPL and media sponsorships.

Ventas is a Chicago-based real estate investment trust specialising in healthcare properties. Its portfolio of roughly 1,400 assets includes senior housing communities, medical office buildings, life science and research space, and hospitals in the US, Canada and the UK, leased to or operated by care providers. Income is rental and operating revenue, with annual revenue about $5bn and a market capitalisation in the tens of billions. Listed on the NYSE (VTR). B2B real estate owner with low consumer awareness.

Alpaca is a San Mateo, California brokerage infrastructure company providing APIs for stock, options and crypto trading, used by fintech apps, banks and developers. Its customers include brokers and apps in the US and Asia, and it earns from payments for order flow, interest and fees. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $763m in total, including a Series D in 2026. Private. Mainly B2B and developer-focused, little consumer awareness.

Optasia is a Dubai-headquartered fintech that offers airtime and data credit, mobile money loans and other financial services through mobile operators and wallet providers in Africa, Asia and the Middle East. It works with telecoms such as MTN, Airtel and Vodacom and serves tens of millions of end users, earning fees from each credit advance. Listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (OPA) in November 2025. Backed earlier by Ardian and other investors. Mostly B2B2C, with low direct brand awareness among end users.

Duetti is a New York music financing and royalty platform that buys music rights and catalogues from artists, labels and rights holders, giving them upfront capital, while investors earn income from royalties. It has acquired catalog interests and offers loans and advances to artists and songwriters, backed by investment firms and about $640m in funding including debt. Private. Mostly known within the music business and fintech circles rather than to general consumers.

Gemini is a New York-based regulated cryptocurrency exchange and custodian, founded in 2014 by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss. It lets retail and institutional customers buy, sell, stake and store digital assets, and offers a crypto rewards credit card in the US. It listed on the Nasdaq (GEMI) in September 2025. Consumer-facing crypto brand with solid US awareness and a record of sports and entertainment marketing.

Payoneer is a New York fintech offering cross-border payment accounts, mass payouts, working capital and card services mainly to small and medium-sized businesses, freelancers and marketplace sellers in emerging markets. It serves around 2 million customers in 190 countries and earns from transaction fees, FX spreads and interest on balances, with revenue near $1bn. It went public via SPAC on Nasdaq (PAYO) in 2021. Mostly B2B/prosumer, known to online sellers and freelancers but not widely to consumers.

U GRO Capital is a Mumbai-based Indian non-bank financial company that lends to small and medium businesses, with a data-driven underwriting platform and co-lending partnerships with banks. Products include secured and unsecured working-capital and machinery loans, and it operates across India with a large branch network. Listed on the NSE and BSE (UGROCAP), with investors such as Samena Capital and Bain Capital-linked funds. B2B lender with low national consumer awareness.

AGNC Investment Corp is a Bethesda, Maryland, internally managed mortgage real estate investment trust that invests mainly in agency residential mortgage-backed securities guaranteed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae. It borrows short-term via repurchase agreements and earns the spread between asset yields and funding costs, paying monthly dividends to shareholders. The portfolio is worth tens of billions of dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (AGNC), founded 2008. Funding shown reflects capital raises. Financial investment vehicle with no consumer brand profile.

Altavair is described by Crunchbase as an asset management firm focused on finance and financial services, headquartered in Issaquah, Washington. The input lists finance and financial services as its industries and shows funding of about $2.4bn with the latest round in June 2026. The exact asset classes, clients and ownership are not given in the input. Likely a specialised asset or lease finance business, but unconfirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Altavair is an asset management firm focused..

about: Bibby Financial Services is a UK-based provider of invoice finance, factoring, asset finance and trade finance to small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Banbury, Oxfordshire, and operating in the UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, the US and Asia. It advances funds against unpaid invoices and earns fees and interest. It is wholly owned by the Bibby Line Group, a family-controlled Liverpool shipping and financial group. Private. B2B lender, known to SMEs, with little consumer profile.

Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, with a legal presence rooted in the Cayman Islands and operations spread globally. It offers spot and derivatives trading, staking, a launchpad, payments, wallets and the BNB Chain ecosystem to well over 250 million registered users. In 2023 it pleaded guilty to US anti-money-laundering charges and paid $4.3bn. Private. Highly known crypto brand; it has used sports sponsorships (such as with Argentina's football team) but faces regulatory sensitivity in many jurisdictions.

Bitdeer Technologies is a Singapore-based Bitcoin mining company and cloud-hash provider, operating large mining data centers in Norway, Bhutan, the US, Ethiopia and elsewhere, and developing its own SEALMINER ASIC miners and AI cloud capacity. Backed by Jihan Wu, co-founder of Bitmain, it earns from mining rewards, hash-rate sales and hosting. Listed on Nasdaq (BTDR) since 2023 via a SPAC merger. Mainly B2B and investor-oriented, with limited consumer brand awareness.

Broadstone Net Lease is a Victor, New York, internally managed REIT that owns single-tenant commercial properties leased on a net basis, covering industrial, healthcare, restaurant, retail and office buildings across the US and Canada, with hundreds of tenants. Income is rental payments, and it pays dividends to shareholders. Listed on the NYSE (BNL) since 2020. Property investor, with no consumer brand profile.

Burford Capital is a litigation finance company, a Guernsey-registered firm with major offices in New York and London, that funds commercial legal claims and arbitrations in exchange for a share of the proceeds. It also manages funds and buys legal assets, notably its large YPF-related Argentine claim. Customers are law firms and corporate claimants. Listed on the NYSE and London markets (BUR), with a portfolio valued in the billions. B2B specialist finance firm, no consumer awareness.

East Money Information is a Shanghai-based Chinese internet financial services company running the Eastmoney.com portal and Tiantian Fund distribution platform, offering financial news, stock data, fund sales, online brokerage through East Money Securities, and wealth products. It serves many millions of retail investors in China. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (300059). A prominent consumer finance brand in China, with little presence abroad.

Emirates Islamic is a Dubai-based Sharia-compliant retail and corporate bank, a subsidiary of Emirates NBD, offering Islamic current and savings accounts, home and auto finance, credit cards, sukuk and business banking in the UAE. It has tens of billions of dirhams in assets and a branch network across the emirates. Owned by Emirates NBD, which is majority-owned by Investment Corporation of Dubai. Well known to UAE consumers, with sports and community sponsorship activity.

ExodusPoint Capital Management is a New York multi-strategy hedge fund founded in 2018 by Michael Gelband, formerly of Millennium, investing across macro, equities, credit and systematic strategies on behalf of institutional investors with tens of billions of dollars under management. It earns management and performance fees. Offices in New York, London, Hong Kong, Singapore and elsewhere. Private. Known within institutional finance, no consumer profile.

IGM Financial is a Winnipeg-based Canadian wealth and asset management company, part of the Power Corporation group, with Investors Group (IG Wealth Management), Mackenzie Investments and Rockefeller Capital Management stakes. It manages about C$300bn of assets for retail investors and advisors and earns fees. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (IGM). Strong Canadian consumer finance brand through advisor networks, and active in sponsorship such as Canadian sport.

Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) is a New Delhi state-owned financing arm of Indian Railways, raising funds on domestic and international bond markets to finance the purchase of rolling stock and railway projects, leasing assets to Indian Railways. It earns lease income and has a loan book around INR 4 trillion. Majority-owned by the Government of India and listed on the NSE and BSE since 2021. Government-linked funding vehicle, no consumer brand marketing.

iwoca is a London online lender providing flexible short-term credit and loans to small businesses in the UK and Germany, using automated underwriting that links to accounting and bank data. It has lent several billion pounds to tens of thousands of SMEs since 2012, and is backed by Augmentum, Santander and Lloyds-linked funds, with debt facilities from Citi and others. Private. Known to small businesses and brokers, with a modest sponsorship record.

Kennedy Wilson is a Beverly Hills, California global real estate investment company that owns, operates and invests in multifamily, office, industrial and hospitality property and loans, mainly in the western US, UK and Ireland. It also manages assets for institutional partners and earns rent, fees and sale gains, with around $20bn of assets under management. Listed on the NYSE (KW), led by William McMorrow. B2B property group with little consumer profile.

Metaplanet is a Tokyo-listed company that has adopted a Bitcoin treasury strategy, holding tens of thousands of BTC on its balance sheet, and also runs a hospitality business and a Bitcoin income business. Often called Japan's MicroStrategy, it funds purchases through equity raises, preferred shares and bonds, and is quoted on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (3350). Led by Simon Gerovich. Retail-investor brand, high online profile in crypto, but no mainstream consumer products.

Neoen is a Paris-based French renewable energy producer developing, financing, building and operating solar, wind and battery storage projects in Australia, France, Finland, the US, Mexico and elsewhere, with over 9 GW in operation or construction. It sells electricity to utilities and corporates under long-term contracts. Acquired by Brookfield Renewable and partners (including Canada's CPP Investments and Mubadala-linked capital) in 2024-25 for around EUR 6bn, and delisted from Euronext. B2B energy firm, little consumer awareness.

Ready Capital is a New York mortgage real estate investment trust and lender that originates and services small-balance commercial loans, SBA 7(a) loans, and multifamily and investor loans, with a large servicing portfolio. Customers are small businesses and property investors. Listed on the NYSE (RC), externally managed by Waterfall Asset Management. B2B finance firm with no consumer brand.

Riot Platforms is a Bitcoin miner based in Castle Rock, Colorado, operating large mining facilities in Rockdale and Corsicana, Texas, plus engineering and data center hosting businesses. It earns by mining Bitcoin and by selling power flexibility to the Texas grid, and holds a large Bitcoin treasury. Listed on Nasdaq (RIOT). B2B and investor-oriented crypto firm, with no consumer brand but some visibility in crypto sponsorship.

STORE Capital was a Scottsdale, Arizona net-lease REIT owning single-tenant operational real estate such as restaurants, health clubs, schools and manufacturing sites, rented to mid-sized businesses. It was acquired in 2023 for about $14bn by GIC and Oak Street Real Estate Capital (Blue Owl) and delisted from the NYSE (STOR). Now privately owned and issuing debt. Landlord business with no consumer brand.

TIAA (Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America) is a New York financial services group offering retirement plans, annuities, wealth management and asset management (Nuveen) mainly to people in academic, medical, research and government fields. It manages over $1.3 trillion in assets, organised as a non-profit-linked mutual-style company. Funding shown reflects capital raises. Established brand among US teachers and non-profit staff; it has sponsored sport in the past.

Tabeo is a London-based UK fintech and payments company providing patient payment and contact management software, mainly for healthcare and professional service providers, according to Crunchbase's financial services and healthcare tags. Funding shown as 750m is probably a debt or facility figure in an unspecified currency. Private. B2B niche payments provider with little consumer awareness. Limited public detail beyond the input.

about: Bilt is a New York rewards and payments company that lets renters earn points on rent payments through the Bilt Mastercard, which has no fee for paying rent, and redeem them for travel, home and other rewards. It has over a million members and a $10.75bn valuation after a 2025 raise. Founded by Ankur Jain, with investors including General Catalyst, Valor and Left Lane. Private. Strong awareness among US renters and credit card enthusiasts.

Carmoola is a London-based UK car finance fintech that offers an online car loan marketplace and budget tool, letting consumers pre-approve finance in minutes and then buy from a dealer. It earns commission and interest, and has raised equity and debt facilities of about GBP 540m, backed by investors including Balderton and Illuminate. Private. Smaller consumer brand with growing awareness among UK car buyers.

ProCap Financial is a New York bitcoin treasury and financial services company launched in 2025, founded by Anthony Pompliano and merged with Columbus Circle Capital I, listed on Nasdaq (BRR). It holds bitcoin on its balance sheet and plans yield products and capital markets services, financed by a PIPE of more than $700m. Investor-facing vehicle, with moderate visibility in crypto circles and none to consumers.

360 Finance (Qifu Technology) is a Shanghai-based Chinese digital consumer finance and credit technology company, spun out of Qihoo 360, connecting borrowers with financial institutions through its app and risk models. It earns platform and technology service fees on loan volumes. Listed on Nasdaq (QFIN). Consumer-facing fintech in China, with limited recognition outside the country.

Masan Group is a Vietnamese consumer and retail conglomerate based in Ho Chi Minh City, owning WinCommerce (WinMart supermarkets), Masan Consumer (Chin-su, Omachi, Nam Ngu sauces), Masan MEATLife and a stake in Techcombank. It sells to Vietnamese households and has revenue near VND 80 trillion. Listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (MSN). Strong, widely advertised consumer brands in Vietnam, and a sports sponsor.

Checkout.com is a London-based global payments company, founded in 2012, which provides card acquiring, payment processing, fraud tools and payouts to merchants like Netflix, eBay, Shein, Sony and Samsung. It handles over $300bn in processed volume and was valued at $40bn in 2022, then marked down to $12bn in 2025. Private. B2B fintech, well known in e-commerce and payments, with its brand showing in sports sponsorship, such as Formula 1 and the Premier League.

Great Rock Capital is a Westport, Connecticut asset-based lender providing senior secured loans to middle-market companies, including retail, consumer and industrial firms, backed by inventory, receivables and equipment. It earns interest and fees, and is owned by Great Rock Capital Partners Management with institutional investors. Private. B2B specialist finance firm with no consumer awareness.

LPL Financial is the largest independent broker-dealer in the US, headquartered in San Diego, Boston and Fort Mill, supporting more than 22,000 financial advisors with brokerage, advisory, custody, research and technology platforms, and about $1.7 trillion in client assets. Revenue is above $10bn. Listed on Nasdaq (LPLA). Advisor-facing brand, advertised to retail investors through its Independent firms, with moderate awareness.

Majid Al Futtaim is a Dubai-based Emirati conglomerate, founded in 1992 by Majid Al Futtaim, that owns and operates the Mall of the Emirates, City Centre malls, Carrefour franchise stores in the Middle East, Africa and Asia, VOX Cinemas, Ski Dubai and Magic Planet, plus retail brands and a consumer finance unit. It employs over 40,000 people, with revenue of roughly $10bn. Privately held by the Majid Al Futtaim family. Very high consumer visibility in the Gulf.

MSCI is a New York provider of investment indexes, analytics, ESG ratings and risk models, including the MSCI World and Emerging Markets indexes, used by asset managers, banks and pension funds worldwide. It earns subscriptions and asset-based fees from index-linked products, with revenue near $3bn. Listed on the NYSE (MSCI). B2B financial data company with strong finance-industry recognition and no general consumer awareness.

The GEO Group is a Boca Raton, Florida operator of private prisons, immigration detention centres, rehabilitation programmes and electronic monitoring services under contract to governments in the US, plus Australia and South Africa. Its largest customers are US federal agencies, such as ICE, and revenue is about $2.4bn. Listed on the NYSE (GEO). Controversial government contractor, low consumer visibility and significant reputational sensitivity for sponsorship.

Waystar is a Louisville, Kentucky healthcare payments software company providing cloud-based revenue cycle tools, claims, patient payments and prior authorisation services to hospitals, health systems and physician groups. Revenue is around $1bn. Listed on Nasdaq (WAY) since its 2024 IPO, controlled by EQT and CPP Investments. B2B software, known to healthcare finance teams, with no consumer awareness.

DANA (Dompet Digital Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based Indonesian digital wallet and payments app, used for QR payments, bill payments, transfers and e-commerce, with tens of millions of users. It is backed by Emtek Group and Ant Group, with a funding figure of about $554m. Private. Strong consumer fintech brand in Indonesia, with heavy promotion and sponsorship in local sports and events.

Aadhar Housing Finance is a Mumbai-based Indian housing finance company providing home loans, mostly to low and middle-income and self-employed customers buying affordable homes, with a network of several hundred branches across India. It earns interest and fees on its loan book. Previously a Wadhwa Group firm, it was acquired by Blackstone in 2019 and listed on the Indian stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) in 2024. Sells to Indian households, moderate regional brand awareness, mostly domestic.

Bit Origin is a New York-based crypto mining company, listed on Nasdaq (BTOG), that mines bitcoin using self-owned machines and hosted facilities in the US. It was formerly a Chinese-linked firm (previously China Xiniya, a footwear and apparel business) that pivoted to digital assets and later announced a Dogecoin treasury strategy. It earns revenue from mining rewards. Small cap, no consumer brand, little public brand awareness outside crypto investors.
cb_desc: Bit Originis an emerging growth crypto mining company.

about: Blue Owl Credit Income is a non-traded private credit fund managed by Blue Owl Capital, based in New York. It raises capital mainly from wealthy individual and retail investors and lends to mid-sized and large US companies through senior secured loans, earning interest income. Blue Owl Capital is a listed alternative asset manager (NYSE: OWL) with well over $200 billion under management. Financial product aimed at investors, little consumer brand awareness; Blue Owl is known in finance circles.

about: Fold is a Phoenix, Arizona fintech offering a bitcoin rewards app and Visa debit and credit cards that pay cashback in bitcoin, plus gift card and bill pay rewards. Customers are US consumers; revenue comes from card interchange and fees. It went public through a SPAC merger with FTAC Emerald in 2025 (Nasdaq: FLD) and holds bitcoin on its balance sheet. Consumer-facing crypto brand with modest awareness among US bitcoin users.

about: Lendistry is a Los Angeles-based lender and fintech and community development financial institution (CDFI) providing loans and capital to small businesses, especially minority-owned and underserved ones, and handled large volumes of PPP loans during the pandemic. Founded in 2015 by Ken Kim and Ray Rodriguez, earning interest and fees, and acquired a bank charter via Lendistry Bank in 2024. US-focused, regional awareness among small business owners.

about: LMAX Group is a London-based financial technology company operating electronic trading venues, including LMAX Exchange for institutional foreign exchange, LMAX Digital for cryptocurrency trading, and FX Clearing. Founded around 2010, it serves brokers, banks, hedge funds and other institutions and earns trading, clearing and technology fees. Regulated in the UK and privately held. B2B finance brand, known in trading circles and with little consumer awareness.

about: meutudo is a Fortaleza, Brazil fintech whose mission is to transform credit access in Brazil. Its app serves mainly retirees, pensioners and public sector workers (INSS beneficiaries) with payroll-deductible loans, credit cards and related services. It earns interest and fees. It has raised a large amount of capital, reported at around $413 million including debt. Consumer financial brand present in Brazil only, with moderate local awareness.

The Crunchbase description says it is a fintech platform that provides customers with financial tools; reported funding is about $424 million, mostly debt, as of April 2026. No further reliable detail is available from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Genting Berhad is a Kuala Lumpur-based Malaysian conglomerate under Lim Kok Thay, with leisure and hospitality (Resorts World Genting casino and theme park, Resorts World Las Vegas, Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore, Genting Malaysia), plantations, power generation and oil and gas operations. It earns revenue from gaming, hotels and cruise lines such as Resorts World Cruises. Listed on Bursa Malaysia (GENTING). Strong consumer visibility in Southeast Asia, including with gaming and entertainment brands.

VakifBank is a large Turkish state-controlled bank based in Istanbul, founded in 1954 and now majority-owned by the Directorate General of Foundations and the Turkey Wealth Fund. It offers retail, commercial, SME and corporate banking, insurance and asset management services via about 900 branches. It is listed on Borsa Istanbul (VAKBN) with total assets above $60 billion and serves millions of customers. High consumer brand recognition in Turkey, with a prominent sponsor of volleyball and sports.

Aditya Birla Capital is the financial services arm of India's Aditya Birla Group, based in Mumbai. It offers lending (Aditya Birla Finance), asset management (Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC), life and health insurance, housing finance and wealth management to retail and corporate customers across India. Listed on the NSE and BSE (ABCAPITAL), with a large loan book and assets under management. Strong brand in India, with the group sponsoring several sports and events.

AmeriGas is a King of Prussia, Pennsylvania propane distributor, one of the largest in the US, supplying home heating, cooking, commercial, industrial and cylinder exchange customers through hundreds of branches. Now part of UGI Corporation, with the former AmeriGas Partners fully merged into UGI in 2019. Customers are residential, commercial and agricultural users across all states. Recognisable on propane cylinder exchange at retail stores; no major sports presence.

Ameriprise Financial is a Minneapolis-based financial services company, spun out of American Express in 2005. It offers financial planning, wealth management, retirement, insurance and asset management (Columbia Threadneedle Investments) through about 10,000 advisors. Assets under management and administration exceed $1.5 trillion, with an NYSE listing (AMP). Customers are affluent retail and institutional investors in the US and abroad. Strong brand recognition in the US, with sponsorship of golf and Ameriprise Invitational events.

Ant International is the Singapore-based international arm of Ant Group, created in 2023, providing digital payments, wallet and fintech services such as Alipay+, Antom, WorldFirst and Bettr. It connects merchants and users across over 100 markets, processing payments for global brands and tourism flows. Owned by Ant Group, an affiliate of Alibaba founder Jack Ma. B2B brand mostly, with the Alipay+ consumer network visible to tourists, and has sponsored sports events.

Bajaj Finserv is a Pune-based Indian financial services holding company in the Bajaj Group, with Bajaj Finance (consumer and SME lending), Bajaj Allianz General and Life Insurance, and Bajaj Finserv Health. Listed on the NSE and BSE (BAJAJFINSV). Serves hundreds of millions of customers in India via EMI cards, loans, and insurance. Strong consumer brand in India.

Barings BDC is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based business development company externally managed by Barings, the asset manager owned by MassMutual. It is a closed-end, publicly traded fund listed on the NYSE (BBDC) that lends to middle-market private companies, earning interest income and distributing it to shareholders. Investors are institutions and retail shareholders, with a portfolio of around $2.5 billion. Financial vehicle, little consumer brand awareness.

Goldman Sachs BDC is a publicly traded business development company (NYSE: GSBD) managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management, based in New York. It lends mainly to US middle-market companies through senior secured loans, earning interest and distributing income to shareholders, with a portfolio of about $3.5 billion. Investors are institutions and retail. The Goldman Sachs name is globally recognised, though the vehicle itself is a financial product with little consumer visibility.

Great-West Lifeco is a Winnipeg-based Canadian financial services holding company that owns Canada Life, Empower (US retirement services) and Irish Life, offering life and health insurance, retirement plans, wealth management and reinsurance to millions of customers in Canada, the US and Europe. Controlled by Power Corporation of Canada and listed on the TSX (GWO). Assets under administration exceed a trillion dollars. Brand known in Canada and Europe through Canada Life and Empower, which have sponsored sports.

Groww is a Bengaluru-based Indian fintech platform, founded in 2016, offering stock broking, mutual funds, F&O trading, IPOs, loans and wealth products to retail investors. It became the largest active investor platform in India, with over 12 million active clients. Backed by Peak XV, Tiger Global, YC and others; it listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2025. Strong consumer app brand among young Indian investors, with active advertising and sponsorship.
